Hypercorrection of Classical Persian بطک (bat̤ak, “duck”), a wanderwort related to Arabic بَطَّة (baṭṭa), بَطّ (baṭṭ) (which itself is from Classical Persian بت (bat), perhaps with the diminutive suffix ـه (-a)), Old Armenian բադ (bad) and Sanskrit वर्तक (vartaka, “quail”), among others. Kogan rejects the दह्यते (dahyate) etymology on the basis that -(j)jh- as a reflex of -hy- is only explainable in those Indo-Aryan languages with a regular change of y to j, which excludes Kashmiri.
